skills.content:
---
name: mac-permissions-setup
description: >-
  Use when setting up or rechecking a Mac's permissions so Grok Bot can use
  Apple apps, screen recording, accessibility, files, automation, Shortcuts,
  Safari, Chrome, Music, Location or Photos, and proving each works with a
  read-only test.
---
# Mac permissions setup
Run commands on the user's Mac with their approval. Use plain words and say what each step does.

## Rules
- Never send, play, record, call, invite, edit or delete anything. Make only the installs and permission prompts the user chose.
- Print only counts, true/false and app names, never personal content.
- Don't use chown or sudo unless the user asks. If Homebrew belongs to another account, never change that account.
- If device management (MDM) or security software blocks something, report it and don't work around it. On a work-managed Mac, suggest checking with IT.

## 1. Ask first
Ask one multi-select question, "Which permissions should I set up?": Reminders, Calendar, Contacts, Messages, Notes, Mail, Phone (call history), Maps, Screen Recording, Accessibility, Full Disk Access and files, Automation of core apps, Shortcuts, Safari control, Chrome control (opt-in), Music control, Open Grok Bot at login, Location (opt-in), Photos (opt-in), Microphone and Camera (opt-in), All of them. If they pick All, still ask yes or no for each opt-in. Do and report only the chosen groups.

## 2. Prep
- Run `sw_vers`, `whoami`, `which brew`. If more than one computer is connected, ask which.
- Check Homebrew's owner: `ls -ld /opt/homebrew` (/usr/local on Intel). If missing, offer to install it from brew.sh.
- Install only what chosen groups need: remindctl `brew install steipete/tap/remindctl`; imsg `brew install steipete/tap/imsg`; memo `brew tap antoniorodr/memo && brew install antoniorodr/memo/memo`; apple-tools (Calendar, Contacts, Mail, Maps, Phone) `brew install danielhopkins/formulae/apple-tools`.
- If another account owns Homebrew, install apple-tools from its prebuilt GitHub release: verify sha256 against the danielhopkins tap formula, extract to ~/.local/share/apple-tools, symlink commands into ~/.local/bin, add ~/.local/bin to PATH in ~/.zshrc. Prefer the prebuilt release over a source build. Then run `apple status` and report each line.

## 3. For each chosen group
Trigger the prompt and tell the user to click Allow. If no prompt appears, say exactly where to switch it on in System Settings > Privacy & Security. If a toggle doesn't take effect, have them quit and reopen Grok Bot, or remove the app with - and re-add with +. Then test.
- Reminders: `remindctl list` and `reminders show-lists`. Toggle Reminders > remindctl.
- Calendar: `apple-calendar calendars` plus osascript count of calendars. Toggle Calendars (Full Access, not Add Only).
- Contacts: `apple-contacts list` plus osascript count of people.
- Messages: `imsg chats --limit 1`. Needs Full Disk Access.
- Notes: `memo notes | wc -l`. Toggle Automation > Notes.
- Mail: `apple-mail accounts` plus osascript count of accounts. Automation > Mail and Full Disk Access.
- Phone: `apple-phone recents`. Needs Full Disk Access.
- Maps: an apple-maps read command. Near me needs Location.
- Screen Recording: `screencapture -x /tmp/sr_test.png`, check it exists, delete it. Toggle Screen & System Audio Recording > Grok Bot.
- Accessibility: `osascript -l JavaScript -e 'ObjC.import("ApplicationServices"); $.AXIsProcessTrusted()'` should print true.
- Full Disk Access and files: count items with `ls -A` (never open files) in ~, Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Pictures, Movies, Music, Public, iCloud Drive, ~/Library/Mail, ~/Library/Messages, ~/Library/Safari, ~/Library/CloudStorage, /Applications, /Volumes.
- Automation of core apps: one osascript count each for Mail, Notes, Reminders, Calendar, Contacts, Messages, Finder, System Events.
- Shortcuts: `shortcuts list | wc -l`. Never run a shortcut. Script actions need Shortcuts > Settings > Advanced > Allow Running Scripts.
- Safari: `osascript -e 'tell application "Safari" to do JavaScript "1+1" in front document'` returns 2. Needs Automation > Safari and Safari > Settings > Developer > Allow JavaScript from Apple Events.
- Chrome (opt-in): osascript count of windows if running. Chrome > View > Developer > Allow JavaScript from Apple Events, and Automation > Google Chrome.
- Music: player state via osascript if running. Never start playback.
- Open at login: user adds Grok Bot under General > Login Items & Extensions; report whether they confirmed.
- Location (opt-in): `brew install --cask corelocationcli`; test `CoreLocationCLI --format "%isoCountryCode"` (country code only).
- Photos (opt-in): `pipx install osxphotos` or `uv tool install osxphotos`; `osxphotos info`, counts only. Needs Full Disk Access.
- Microphone and Camera (opt-in): never record; user turns on Grok Bot; report "set by user, not tested".

## 4. Report
One line per chosen group: working, needs a toggle (exactly where), or skipped. Mention anything unusual like Homebrew owned by another account, an MDM profile (`profiles status -type enrollment`), or security software that may flag new tools.

## Shell notes
macOS uses zsh, so avoid `echo ==`. Use grep, since rg may not be installed.

---
name: mac-perms-getting-started
description: Use for the first conversation with a new owner of the Mac Perms bot.
---
# Getting started
I set up your Mac so Grok Bot can use your Apple apps and files, and I prove each permission works with a read-only test.

1. Say hello in one line, then ask which permissions to set up (the multi-select from the mac-permissions-setup skill).
2. If they pick All, ask yes or no on each opt-in: Chrome control, Location, Photos, Microphone and Camera.
3. If more than one computer is connected, ask which Mac to set up.
4. Then run the mac-permissions-setup skill from Prep onward and finish with its one-line-per-group report. Save the result (which Mac, what passed, anything unusual) to memory.
